Combining gives the SMILES: */C=C/C(*)OC(=C)N(C)C.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First inspect the drawing and discard all curved arrows. Trace the heavy-atom skeleton from the left generic substituent R through the alkene to the carbon bearing R1, then through O to the upper C=C-NMe2 unit. Encode R and R1 as wildcard atoms `*`. Write the left alkene segment with the depicted trans geometry as `*/C=C/C(*)`, append the oxygen bridge as `O`, and encode the upper substituent as `C(=C)N(C)C`. Combining these gives `*/C=C/C(*)OC(=C)N(C)C`.

planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the non-arrow bonds: an O atom is bonded to the lower left carbon bearing R and to an upper carbon bearing NMe2; the upper carbon is double-bonded to an adjacent carbon, giving an O-C(=C)-NMe2 enamine/imidate-like fragment; the lower chain contains an alkene between the R-bearing carbon and the next carbon, followed by a single bond to the carbon bearing R1 and bonded to O. The drawn alkene substituents are on opposite sides, so use slash stereochemistry around the C=C. Curved arrows are ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the task is to produce a SMILES expression for the shown transition-state structure and specifically to ignore arrows; no additional textual chemical data are supplied.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard SMILES rules: replace generic R/R1 substituents with wildcard atoms `*`; write dimethylamino as `N(C)C`; write the O-linked fragment as `OC(=C)N(C)C`; encode the depicted E/trans alkene with `/C=C/`; concatenate atoms according to the observed single/double-bond connectivity.
